evidence.text: Every Q3 2026 scenario input printed above the FY scenario Eni used on 29 July to set its EUR15bn CFFO guide and EUR3.4bn buyback (Brent $85, SERM $14, TTF EUR50/MWh): Brent averaged $97.0, TTF averaged $21.5/MMBtu (about EUR63/MWh), and TotalEnergies' European refining marker was $33.2/b against $13.5 in Q2. Brent was still around $100 in mid-October. Eni's published policy pays 100% of the CFFO increment as an extraordinary dividend in Q4 when Brent is above $90 or refining margins are 50%+ above budget, with the decision due 'in October'. Using Eni's own sensitivities (EUR0.11bn per $1 Brent, EUR0.08bn per $1 SERM), FY Brent near $95 and FY SERM near $13-15 give an increment of roughly EUR1.1-1.4bn. The street expects about EUR1bn (Equita) and FY CFFO of about EUR16bn. The Plenitude deconsolidation (completed 1 October) and the $2bn Ares capital expected in Q3 also push gearing below the 10% floor, which supports a buyback upsize on top.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Distribution news has driven the last three prints. Q3 2025: shares rose on a buyback upsize (https://sweetcrudereports.com/eni-ups-buyback-on-strong-q3-results-shares-rise/). Q1 2026: about +1% despite an earnings miss, because the buyback rose to EUR2.8bn (https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/eni-gli-analisti-conti-sotto-le-attese-ma-convincono-il-buyback-a-2-8-miliardi-e-le-stime-sulla-202604241117072364). Q2 2026: +4.5% intraday Milan on an 11% beat plus a buyback raise to EUR3.4bn (https://quifinanza.it/economia/finanza/eni-vola-borsa-trimestrale-utile-buyback-dividendo-2026/1010238/). The baseline's own 8-move history is monthly 6-K noise and was not used.
evidence.why_not_priced: The direction is partly priced: the stock is at its 52-week high, +7.6% over 20 days, and Equita's EUR1bn special is in circulation. What is not visibly priced is the size of the special. Money.it's widely read calculation (2026-10-06) puts it at EUR640m, counting only the SERM leg at the July $14 scenario. Applying the policy's Brent-above-$90 leg to the realised Q3 tape adds about EUR0.4-0.6bn. If the market had priced EUR1.2bn+, the preview pieces would quote it rather than EUR0.64-1bn. The risk is the other way too: Eni may pay only part now and defer the rest as 'depending on how long the scenario lasts'.
evidence.independence: TotalEnergies Q3 2026 indicators, 2026-10-14 (https://investingnews.com/totalenergies-se-third-quarter-2026-main-indicators/; Brent 97.0, TTF 21.5, ERM 33.2). evidence.text: Peer updates point to a large sequential refining step-up for Eni's Q3. TotalEnergies' European refining marker went from $13.5 to $33.2/b (+146%), with R&C cash flow guided about $2bn higher QoQ, and Shell put Q3 refining margins at a record $42 vs $24. Eni's Q2 SERM was $8.3/b, which earned refining EBIT of EUR80m. Scaling by the peer marker implies a Q3 SERM near $20, worth roughly +EUR0.2bn of quarterly refining EBIT (EUR0.02bn per $1 per quarter). That roughly offsets the Brent drop ($104.5 to $97, about -EUR0.2bn quarterly CFFO), and higher TTF (+EUR0.1bn) is upside to GGP. The Q3 adjusted net bridge from Q2's EUR2.33bn therefore lands around EUR2.45-2.55bn, at or slightly above the EUR2.48bn company consensus.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 beat consensus by about 11% and the stock rose +4.5% intraday, with the buyback raised the same day. Q1 2026 missed by about 14% (1.3 vs 1.51 per WallStreetItalia) and still rose about 1% on the buyback. The quarter's number has mattered less than distributions.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. BofA notes that the majors' Q3 trading updates lifted sector estimates about 5%, and the company-compiled EUR2.48bn is above Q2's EUR2.33bn. The residual upside is that Eni's refining is small and was loss-making a year ago, so consensus models may under-scale the SERM jump. If fully priced, the company consensus would sit nearer EUR2.6bn (where VA already is).
evidence.independence: Proxy. It shares the TotalEnergies and Shell series with the capital-return finding above. Eni itself has published no Q3 SERM. The Shell Q3 update is the independent confirmation of the margin step-up (https://www.hl.co.uk/shares/stock-market-news/company--news/shell-sees-record-q3-refining-margins,-lifts-gas-production-estimate).

evidence.text: BofA (2026-10-16) sits below Visible Alpha consensus on Eni's Q3: adjusted net EUR2.5bn vs EUR2.6bn (-3%), adjusted EBIT EUR3.5bn vs EUR3.8bn (-8%, flat QoQ). BofA attributes the EBIT gap mostly to the Searah JV (Indonesia/Malaysia, with Petronas) no longer contributing to consolidated EBIT. Any wire headline comparing consolidated EBIT with an un-updated consensus could therefore read as a miss.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean prior on a perimeter-driven EBIT miss. Q1 2026's headline miss was bought on the buyback (about +1%).
evidence.why_not_priced: The VA consensus at EUR2.6bn sits above the company's own EUR2.48bn, so part of the street carries a higher net bar than the company-compiled one. A print near EUR2.5bn reads as in line against Eni's consensus and as a slight miss against VA. Which bar the wires use on the day is not knowable in advance. BofA still raised its target (to EUR24.5, below spot of about EUR26.1), so it is not a negative call.
evidence.independence: None. This is a single-bank read. Eni's own Q2 release confirms that Searah was set up in Q2 as a 50/50 JV (equity-accounted), which supports the perimeter mechanism (https://www.eni.com/content/dam/enicom/documents/press-release/migrated/2026-it/07/CS-risultati-secondo-trimestre-2026.pdf).

first_hunter_context.bar: Q3 2026 revenue $210-220M company guide (Q2 release 2026-07-23, https://www.01net.it/maxlinear-inc-announces-second-quarter-2026-financial-results/). Consensus $214.95M revenue / $0.56 non-GAAP EPS (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MXL/earnings/), with Benzinga at about $211.2M / $0.51 (snippet only, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/MXL/earnings-forecasts). The guide and two sources roughly agree, so the bar is sourced. Q4 2026 consensus is about $222.6M revenue (Benzinga snippet only, single source, unverified). EarningsWhispers' $171.6M is stale (pre-guide) and is disowned. The last 6 quarters' revenue beats ran 0-2.6% (MarketBeat table).
first_hunter_context.positioning_check: Short interest 4.89M shares, 5.84% of float, 1.49 days to cover at the 2026-09-30 settlement. It has risen 5 reports running (4.17M at 7/31) but is not crowded (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MXL/short-interest/). Skew is +3.82 vol pts (downside paid, mild); put/call OI 0.67. The stock is down 16.4% in 5 days, 23.4% in 20 days and 49% off its 52-week high, into a sector sell-off (SOX about -12% in the week to 10-14 on Broadcom/Intel CEO capital warnings). Insiders: CEO Seendripu sold about 591k shares (~$50M) over 6 months, with Forms 4 on 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-01; FMR cut 68.6% in Q2.

evidence.text: The Street's Q4 2026 revenue bar is about $222.6M, only +3.5% q/q on a ~$215M Q3. Management's own forward commentary points above that: on the Q2 call it said there would be no 'stairstep', with optical volumes rising as more customers enter production and visibility of about six months, and Q1-27 orders already being placed. At Citi TMT (scheduled 2026-09-09) it said customer orders/forecasts cover next year, lead times are 26-28 weeks and pricing stays firm through end-2027. The 10-Q shows inventory +35% to $105.5M, with WIP up from $47.6M to $79.0M since December, plus restricted cash tied to purchase obligations. This corroborates a ramp rather than a stall, so a Q4 guide midpoint in the $230-240M area would clear the bar.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide is what moves this name. April 2026: Q2 guide well above Street, +76.1%. July 2026: Q3 guide of $210-220M against ~$175M Street still fell -21.5%, after a ~22% run into the print. So a strong guide has paid once and been sold once. 5 of the last 7 reactions were down.
evidence.why_not_priced: The Q4 consensus of +3.5% q/q sits far below the Q2-to-Q3 step (+27%) and below management's 'continued rise' language. If the market expected a big Q4 step, the 20-day tape would not show -23% into the print, and the event-implied move would not be netted down to 7%. However, the Q4 consensus figure is single-source (Benzinga snippet), so this is capped.
evidence.independence: 10-Q inventory/WIP build (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1288469/000128846926000051/mxl-20260630.htm, 2026-07-23) and the Citi TMT summary (https://quartr.com/events/maxlinear-inc-mxl-citi-s-2026-global-tmt-conference_ozX1H5eK; conference scheduled 2026-09-09 per the company's 2026-08-17 release, Quartr labels it 2026-10-06). Q4 consensus is from Benzinga (snippet). Caveat: at Citi, management reiterated the FY optical midpoint of $220M rather than raising it, which limits the optical upside.

evidence.text: MXL goes into this print after a sector-driven de-rating rather than a run-up. It is -16.4% over 5 days and -23.4% over 20 days. The cause is a sector-wide sell-off: optical names fell on 10-15 ('rotation into defensives', no company news), and the SOX fell ~12% in the week to 10-14 after Broadcom's Hock Tan and Intel's Lip-Bu Tan said capital, not chips, is AI's constraint, while Hock Tan said demand exceeds supply through 2029. In July, by contrast, the stock ran ~22% into the print and fell 21.5% on a beat-and-raise. No MXL-specific negative 8-K, PR or downgrade appears since July 23 (EDGAR shows only Forms 4/144/13G).
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: July 2026: up ~22% into the print, then -21.5% on beat-and-raise. April 2026: entered depressed and moved +76%. That is two observations consistent with run-in mattering, which is not a base rate.
evidence.why_not_priced: The de-rating is the price. The claim is about the reaction function: a lower bar into a print where the company-level demand commentary has not changed. If the market had priced a demand problem at MXL specifically, short interest would be building faster (it is +1% in the last report, DTC 1.5) and skew would be steeper than +3.8 vol pts.
evidence.independence: Broadcom/Intel CEO remarks, 2026-10-12 (https://finviz.com/news/401102/broadcom-ceo-sees-capital-as-main-constraint-on-ai-growth-despite-easing-chip-shortages); Quiver 2026-10-12 says the -6.9% day had no company-specific news (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/MaxLinear+Slides+as+Recent+Rally+Loses+Steam+Ahead+of+Earnings). This is an inference about reaction, not a company number.

evidence.text: Optical counterparties that reported after MXL last spoke (2026-07-23) describe continuing strong demand. Credo's FQ1-27 (reported 2026-09-02, quarter ended 2026-08-01) had revenue of $479M (+115% y/y), a record optical DSP quarter and a guide of $525-535M. Eoptolink's H1 report (2026-08-25) had Q2 revenue +50.8% q/q, and brokers cite high Q3/Q4 order visibility. Neither shows an air pocket in 800G module/DSP demand during MXL's Q3.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: MXL has beaten revenue consensus by 0-2.6% in each of the last 6 quarters (MarketBeat), and the reactions to those beats were mostly negative.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced. It rules out a demand-collapse reading of the 23% drawdown rather than adding new upside. These are proxies: Credo competes with MXL, and module makers are customers but unnamed.
evidence.independence: Eoptolink H1 2026 (https://m.c114.com.cn/w123-1316262.html, 2026-08-25). It is a different company and document, but the same industry proxy.

evidence.text: The Silicon Motion SIAC arbitration (claim: $160M termination fee plus further damages) has had its hearings concluded (October 2025 and March 2026), and the parties are awaiting a final award. One call summary expected a decision in 2H 2026. MXL had $64.8M of unrestricted cash, a $125M term loan and negative H1 operating cash flow (-$4.1M) at 6/30. An adverse award disclosed in the Q3 release or 10-Q would force a financing question. No award has been reported by either party as of 10-22, so this is a low-probability tail inside the window.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: There has been no award in the history. The matter has been a disclosed risk factor since 2023.
evidence.why_not_priced: Arbitration is confidential under SIAC rules, so an award could sit undisclosed until a periodic filing. The market is not visibly pricing a $160M+ charge against a $6bn market cap with $65M cash: skew is only +3.8 vol pts.
evidence.independence: MXL 10-Q liquidity figures (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1288469/000128846926000051/mxl-20260630.htm, 2026-07-23) and the SIMO FY2025 20-F (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001329394/000119312526197184/d17718d20f.htm). Same matter, so this is one finding.

evidence.text: The CEO sold about 591k shares (~$50M) in the 6 months to October, with Forms 4 filed 2026-08-18 and 2026-09-01 after Form 144s on 8/14 and 8/17. Insiders made 25 sales and 0 purchases. FMR cut its stake 68.6% in Q2.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is largely priced: these are public Forms 4. It is filed because it bears on how holders read a beat.

evidence.why_not_priced: It lands inside the company's guided range, so it is mostly expected and sized toward 0.

evidence.text: Signs of wireless pricing discipline. Desjardins (2026-09-14 upgrade to Buy) and management at CIBC both say back-to-school discounting was quiet or lighter. evidence.text: The CRTC ban on activation and modification fees took effect 2026-06-12, so Q3 is the first full quarter without them. Q2 mobile phone ARPU was already -2% (C$54.25 vs 55.45). FY FCF tracks the middle to upper half of C$4.1-4.3B, which leaves room to narrow EBITDA/FCF toward the top.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The FCF guide raise and capex cut in Q1'26 sent the shares up >11% intraday (rbr.com 2026-04-22). A reaffirmed guide in Q2'26 came with -4.1%.

evidence.text: The May 2026 global offering (about 77.8m new share-equivalents: 58.05m common + 1.97m ADSs x 10, roughly +9% on the Q1 average 859.0m shares, about US$269m gross) lands for a full quarter in Q3. Q2 already showed Vesta FFO per share -1.8% YoY and FFO after tax per share -26.2% with only part of a quarter of dilution, so Q3 FFO per share is likely flat-to-down YoY against Q3 2025's US$47.4m FFO on about 868m shares. The money funds a 1.78m sf development pipeline at a 10.1% expected yield (22.3% pre-leased) plus land, so it is growth funding, not distress.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (first per-share dilution print, FFO/share -1.8%): -1.0%. Q1 2026 (FFO -4.1% YoY on lower interest income): +2.3%. This name has not been punished hard on FFO per share.
evidence.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the share count and the Q2 per-share decline are public. What is left is the size of a full-quarter per-share decline on a name that trades on FFO yield, at a moment when the stock has run up into the print.
evidence.independence: Same document as finding 1 (Q2 6-K), used for a different line (per-share vs revenue). Share count for Q1 from https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001969373/000196937326000013/quarterlyreport1q2026ex-991.htm

evidence.text: On 2026-09-09 Vesta prepaid US$105m of private debt early (US$60m 5.31% notes due 2027-09, US$45m 5.85% term loan due 2028-05), paying make-whole amounts in Q3. That puts a one-off finance charge, not quantified in the release, into Q3, and removes about US$5.8m a year of interest from Q4 on. S&P (2026-08-21) and Fitch (2026-08-31) both upgraded Vesta to BBB/stable. Financing question answered: the cash comes from the May equity raise and the move simplifies the structure. It is not distress, so this nets to about zero.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured. The 6-K days after the upgrades and the prepayment moved -1.2% (08-24), -0.58% (08-31) and +0.24% (09-09) per the baseline's non-earnings rows.
evidence.why_not_priced: The make-whole cost is unquantified and will appear in Q3 finance costs, a below-operating-income one-off, so it can blur the reported FFO by a cent-fraction. The rating upgrades and the prepayment themselves are public and priced.
evidence.independence: Fitch upgrade 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1969373/000095010326013269/dp252701_ex9901.htm. S&P upgrade 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1969373/000095010326012775/dp252171_ex9901.htm

evidence.text: Positioning into the print: VTMX rose from 33.87 (10-09) to 36.72 (10-20) and sat at 35.99 on 10-22, +9.97% over 20 sessions and 2.6% below its 52-week high, on thin ADR turnover (about 64k shares a day per the baseline). A good part of a positive print is in the price; the last print with no guide change was sold -1.0%.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 came after a flat tape and fell -1.0%. Q4 2025 came after a flat tape (33.6-33.7) and rose +6.9%. No case in the sample of a print following a 10% run-up.
evidence.why_not_priced: This is the price itself, not an unpriced fact. It is filed to offset the guidance finding: the run-up is what pricing-in of a raise would look like.
evidence.independence: Sealed baseline tape (run_up_20d_pct 9.97, pct_from_52w_high -2.61).

evidence.text: Inside Q2, which the CEO letter did not discuss, Bajío stabilized occupancy fell from 96.0% to 92.2%, Bajío same-store from 95.8% to 94.2%, North same-store from 97.1% to 93.0%, and Bajío vacant sf rose to 2.11m (10.3%), while total occupancy rose on lease-up of new product. If those regional slides continue in Q3, same-store NOI growth (+5.9% in Q2) and the occupancy headline could disappoint.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026, the print that carried these declines, moved -1.0%.
evidence.why_not_priced: It is in the July filing's tables, not in the wire copy or the call summaries, which led with the +200bp total occupancy. Segment net of the rest: Monterrey (>80%), Mexico City and Central SE (100%) and new deliveries carried the total, so this is sized small and net.
evidence.independence: Same document as findings 1 and 3. FIBRA Prologis's weak same-store cash NOI of +1.7% in Q3 (finding 2's document) points the same way on same-store momentum.

evidence.text: The US did not extend USMCA and moves to annual reviews through 2036 (El CEO, 2026-10-06), with a USTR public consultation open to January. Vesta's Q2 letter already called the July 1 review 'continuity, but not resolution'. Management will be asked about tenant decision delays on the 10-23 call.
evidence.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 2026 call flagged USMCA uncertainty and the stock moved -1.0%. The stock has risen about 10% since the 10-06 article, so the market has looked through it.
evidence.why_not_priced: Largely priced: a macro headline every holder knows. The residual is any company-specific statement of leasing delays on the call. Macro-to-company transmission is not confirmed by the company, so this is a proxy.
